title: Four agreements, including the Energy Services Agreement
who: The City Council, sitting as the Pittsburg Power Company board
source: Interview with City Manager Darin Gale, transcript p. 6

title: The water system
detail: Delta Diablo wants the cooling system plans before it issues a construction permit
source: Delta Diablo–AVAIO recycled water emails, p. 4 (Max David, April 13, 2026) and pp. 1-2 (June 9, 2026)

title: Permits for the 37 diesel generators
who: The Bay Area Air Quality Management District’s executive officer
detail: Appeals go to a separate Hearing Board
source: BAAQMD responses to Scot Scoop, p. 1

title: 45-day emergency moratorium on new data centers
detail: Adopted unanimously Oct. 26, effective immediately; Phase 1 is exempt. Expires Dec. 10 unless extended.
source: Urgency ordinance (Oct. 26, 2026), §2.A.iv (Phases II and III are subject to it) and §7 (effective immediately, in effect for 45 days unless extended under Gov. Code §65858); City of Pittsburg news release; Contra Costa News, Oct. 27, 2026

title: Consent to a canal easement
who: The Contra Costa Water District’s elected board
detail: The district applies to the bureau only after this vote
source: CCWD email, Jewel Jacobson to Ryan Bernal and John DeLacio, “Pittsburg Data Hub - Info for Pre-Application Meeting” (undated): “CCWD will submit the SF299 after CCWD’s Board of Directors consents to the Bureau issuing a Temporary Construction in Advance of Easement and eventual granting of permanent easement(s)”

title: Federal environmental review
detail: Required for the easement, the water district has told AVAIO
source: CCWD project review letter No. 4 (Aug. 28, 2025), p. 3; CCWD comment letter (April 15, 2024), p. 1; Kimley-Horn email to CCWD (Ryan Bernal, April 25, 2025: “CEQA/NEPA environmental documentation that will be required for construction of the improved crossing”)

title: The easement for a road and utility lines
detail: Only the bureau can grant it. No road reaches the land south of the canal.
source: Bureau of Reclamation email (Michael Inthavong, May 18, 2026: “Only Reclamation can issue an easement”); AVAIO memo responses to Reclamation (June 4, 2026), pp. 3 and 7

title: Approval of the buildings
who: The zoning administrator, a single city official
detail: Under the specific plan, projects that fit it “shall not require additional environmental review” beyond effects peculiar to them.
source: Draft Program EIR (July 2024), p. 2.0-17; interview with Darin Gale, transcript p. 12

detail: Gale says proposals would go to the Planning Commission and council instead, but the plan hasn’t been amended to require that.
source: Interview with Darin Gale, transcript p. 12
